title: How to Fine-Tune BERT for Text Classification?
problem: Although BERT has achieved amazing results in many natural language understanding (NLU) tasks, its potential has yet to be fully explored.
There is little research to enhance BERT to improve the performance on target tasks further.
The first problem of applying BERT to text classification is how processing the text with a length larger than 512.
Catastrophic forgetting (McCloskey and Cohen, 1989) is usually a common problem in transfer learning, which means the pre-trained knowledge is erased during learning of new knowledge.
core_techniques: [4.2] Within-task pre-training | 타깃 과제의 학습 데이터로 BERT를 추가 사전학습하는 방법
[4.2] In-domain pre-training | 동일 도메인의 데이터로 BERT를 추가 사전학습하는 방법
[4.2] Cross-domain pre-training | 동일 및 다른 도메인의 데이터를 함께 사용해 추가 사전학습하는 방법
[4.3] Multi-task Fine-Tuning | 여러 관련 과제를 동시에 학습하면서 BERT를 멀티태스크 방식으로 미세조정하는 방법
[4.1] head+tail | 긴 문서에서 앞 128개와 뒤 382개 토큰을 선택하는 절단 방식
[4.1] layer-wise learning rate | 하위 층에 더 작은 학습률을 적용하는 층별 감소 학습률

contributions: [1] We propose a general solution to fine-tune the pre-trained BERT model, which includes three steps: (1) further pre-train BERT on within-task training data or in-domain data; (2) optional fine-tuning BERT with multi-task learning if several related tasks are available; (3) fine-tune BERT for the target task. We also investigate the fine-tuning methods for BERT on target task, including preprocess of long text, layer selection, layer-wise learning rate, catastrophic forgetting, and low-shot learning problems. We achieve the new state-of-the-art results on seven widely-studied English text classification datasets and one Chinese news classification dataset.
